# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 48 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 48 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_048_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 12, Part 5 — The Conclusion of the Mandates

**48:1** When I had finished writing all the commandments, he said to me: "Now I have given you all these commandments, and you shall keep them and shall walk in them. And you shall walk in them if your heart is pure toward God. And you shall keep them if you do not add any evil desire from the world to them, for it is not I, but the Lord who grants you this."

**48:2** "But if your heart is always turned toward God, you shall overcome all these things and all things are possible to you. But if you turn away from God and are double-minded, know that not one of these things shall be possible for you. For the man who is turned away from God shall not be able to keep them, and shall be delivered to death."

**48:3** "But I say to you, Hermas: these things that I say are not my own words, but the words of God, whom I serve. Keep them and you shall live. I speak to you not only for myself but for all men who shall repent and do these things."

**48:4** "For if you keep them you shall live and have peace with all men, and all shall live in peace with you who keep them. Therefore, I charge you again: keep them diligently, obey them, and do not slack. For if you do these things you shall live; if you do not do them you shall die."

**48:5** "When I had heard these commandments, I went away from him greatly shaken and afraid, and thought within myself: if even this man who keeps the commandments shall with difficulty be saved, what shall become of those who do not keep them? And many cares and anxieties came upon me. But he said to me: 'Do not worry about these things, but be strong and do good, and you shall receive great glory.'"

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the solemn closing charge of the Mandates section.*
